main_text.p: st. preciosior in conscientia sua erat sacra Dei lex & sanctio, quàm ut pauperie vel gentili-ùm fauore induceretur ad illicita obeunda; sicut & Daniel cum socijs in Babylone, Joseph in Ægypto, Judith in castris Holofernis, Gen.43.Judith 12. Omnia quidem munda sunt mundis. Verùm legis Mosaicæ ritus usque ad Christum Judæis omnibus ob-servandus erat, & idolatriæ occasio summa diligentia evitanda. Polluebantur igitur Israelitæ ferè omnes, i.e. plurimi contra legem agendo, quam Tobias summopere semper observare satagebat, ne peccaret in Deum, & contra conscientiam illicita sumeret, cum licita per Dei gratiam non deessent. Atque huius sanctitatis præmium Tobias etiam in hoc mundo accepit. Donatus est enim a rege Salmanasar libertate, ut illi licuerit pergere & operari, ut voluit. Sed ipse hac sua libertate, ex gratia Dei (cuius opera & ferræ, & tyranni mansuefieri, velint nolint, coguntur) accepta, non abusus est: sed iti-tans ad omnes captiuos, eos salutariter monuit atque confolatus est. Porrò quæ salutis monita fuerint, quæ illis dedit Tobias, videris in commentarijs Pellicani. Exhortatus enim est concaptiuos ad tolerantiam exilij, ad obedientiam regi præstândam, etiamsi immo destior & discolus iam eis contigisset, quado id Domino placuisse viderent ex facto, pœnam esse codignam criminibus non possent ignorare: forti animo omne solum patriam

page.notes: The running head "NVPTIALES." and the page number "191" are read from a small-capital, partly worn print; check them. The opening fragment "st." (from "est") is cut off at the line start and stays a fragment. Doubtful readings: "Gen.43." (the number after "Gen." is faint); "ferræ" in "ferè" line, and "si" in "etiamsi" and "destior" (printed "destior", kept as printed); "quado" is printed as such and kept. Words corrected only by the u/v and i/j rules: vsque, Judæis, Iudith, Ioseph, Christum, evitanda, concaptiuos. The punctuation "obeunda;" and "abusus est:" is taken from the scan as printed. The line "tans ad omnes captiuos" begins with "iti-" at the line end, kept with its printed hyphen. A small star mark near the foot is a printer's or scan mark, not text, and is left out.
